OPEN DIRECTIONS for the manager (all OUTSIDE this brief's two named approaches, hence surfaced not pursued): (1) LIFT THE 1-BLOCK/SM OCCUPANCY -- the only profile-identified lever. FP32 176x176 = 123.9KB > 114KB (=228/2) so 2 blocks/SM is structurally blocked while the WHOLE matrix is resident. A megakernel variant that keeps only the active region resident (evict finalized columns [0,j) to global as R+v, hold only [j,n)) could drop peak SMEM under 114KB late in the factorization, but peak at j=0 is still full-matrix -- needs a 2-phase or half-precision-staging design. (3) Raise MAXCB>32 (brief 25's noted lever) so the blocked path uses cb=44 (4 panels vs 6) -- cuts (a)'s launch count but touches the shared C++ panel buffers (red[MAXCB*16]/wsh[MAXCB]) and all blocked-path n.
